title: Financial-data vendors — what they expose
caption: What each vendor publishes over MCP and APIs, what it sells, and how a client gets it · read 2026-10-04 · ➕ Extra: not on the CCAR-F exam · not investment or procurement advice
noPriceNote: No price appears on this page: none of the pages I read states one. Where a page did not say something, the table says “not stated”.
glanceNote: MCP = a server an AI agent connects to and calls tools on. API = the vendor's own web or library interface for programs. “Not stated” means the vendor's page did not say.

basis.meaning: Read on the vendor's own page
From a search summary of the vendor's page; the page itself could not be fetched

glance.mcp: `https://mcp.crunchbase.com` · 14 tools: natural-language answers, structured search, entity profiles, saved lists
glance.api: REST `https://api.crunchbase.com/v4/data/` · JSON · API key in a header · 200 calls per minute
glance.sells: Private-company data: company profiles, funding rounds, people, investors, acquisitions, plus predictions
glance.access: MCP: sign in with your Crunchbase account. MCP is bought per workspace and assigned to each user as a seat; ask Crunchbase sales. API: an API key

glance.mcp: `https://mcp.zoominfo.com/mcp` · 19 tools listed on docs.gtm.ai: search, enrich and research companies and contacts; intent, scoops, news; audiences

glance.sells: B2B company and contact data: firmographics, technographics, funding, business signals, contact details
glance.access: A ZoomInfo licence (self-serve or enterprise); OAuth sign-in; plan limits and credits apply; a free trial is offered

facts.topic: MCP tools (14 on its Tool Reference page)
facts.text: Expert: `cb_expert_query_answer`, `cb_expert_build_search`, `cb_expert_query_domain`, `cb_expert_resolve_entity`, `cb_expert_submit_feedback`. Structured: `cb_reference`, `cb_entity_autocomplete`, `cb_entity_get`, `cb_search_query`. Lists: `cb_list_query`, `cb_list_create`, `cb_list_add_entities`, `cb_list_get`. Utility: `cb_metering_get_state`
Claude, ChatGPT, VS Code with GitHub Copilot, Perplexity, Mistral Vibe, and any client that implements the current MCP specification
Entity lookup, search and autocomplete families; example path `/entities/organizations/crunchbase`; HTTPS only; key as the `user_key` parameter or the `X-cb-user-key` header
790 data fields per company; 15 million+ private-company predictions refreshed weekly (as stated on the product page)

OAuth 2.0 sign-in through a browser, with ZoomInfo credentials or company single sign-on. Clients named: Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Cursor, VS Code Copilot, Claude, ChatGPT, Perplexity. The docs say model training should be turned off in the AI client
Search: contacts, companies, intent, news, scoops. Enrich: contacts, companies, corporate hierarchy, intent, news, org charts, scoops, technologies, hashtags. Lookup. Usage
Intent endpoints need “the Intent SKU” in your package
The REST base URL and the rate-limit numbers were not on the pages I fetched. The old API documentation is marked “Legacy”

Its “Enterprise MCP” article lists “eight content APIs”: Fundamentals, Estimates, Ownership, M&A, Pricing (FGP), People, Events and Supply Chain. The same article discusses OAuth and scoped access for MCP in general; it does not describe FactSet's own enforcement

The endpoint URL and 11 tool names appear in a search summary (which also cites third-party listings), not on a FactSet page I could read, so they carry 🔎. The developer-portal pages are script-built and returned only a title to my fetch. A search summary mentions 24 tools and a trial by contacting FactSet; I could not confirm either on FactSet's page

sources.label: FactSet Enterprise MCP, part 3 (security and governance)

facts.text: “FactSet's corporate governance database, SharkRepellent, provides takeover defense and corporate governance data for thousands of US companies.” It compiles board structure and shareholder-rights data from articles of incorporation, bylaws, state takeover laws and shareholder rights plans, tracks poison pills, and scores defences with a “Bullet Proof Rating System”
Not stated. The page mentions custom reports and company defence profiles. A FactSet marketplace page for “FactSet Corporate Governance” returned only its title
I found no MCP server or API for SharkRepellent on the pages I read, and none of FactSet's MCP content areas is governance data
`findEntity`, `searchEntityDocuments`, `getEntityRatings`, `getEntityRatingDrivers`, `getEntityScorecard`
“Request credentials and endpoint URL from Moody's”; OAuth through a Moody's login page. Works with any LLM that supports the MCP standard, including Claude and OpenAI APIs
Moody's names three: “Smart APIs”, MCP servers, and integrations through Databricks Marketplace and Claude for Financial Services
600 million entities and 2 billion ownership links (Moody's press release); 600 million+ public and private entities (Moody's blog)

Financial statements and line items; market prices and price charts; segment financials, market capitalisation, total enterprise value; company intelligence; competitors; M&A transactions; earnings-call transcripts. Private-company financials were “coming soon” and Capital IQ consensus estimates “in development” when the post was written
Kensho, S&P Global's AI hub, for the Kensho LLM-ready API. S&P's press release says it works with any large language model
The MCP endpoint URL, the tool names and the licence terms. S&P's own “AI for partners and developers” page returned an access error

Kensho — LLM-ready API and MCP server access

facts.text: Only search summaries of S&P's pages: RatingsDirect covers credit ratings and research, is integrated into the Capital IQ platform, and S&P offers data feeds, cloud and API solutions (XpressAPI, Capital IQ API)
RatingsDirect and the S&P marketplace pages returned access errors or only a title when fetched, so no endpoint, protocol or licence detail is shown

Fitch Nexus gives access to Fitch Ratings credit research, current and historical ratings, outlooks and watch changes, company financials, forecasts and key ratios, and rating factors and sensitivities. CreditSights insights are “available soon”; BMI and Sustainable Fitch follow “in the following months”. It is described as built for “enterprise and regulated environments”
Fitch's own domains (fitchratings.com, fitchsolutions.com) were blocked to my tools, and the business-wire copy returned an access error. This row rests on a republished press release

facts.topic: APIs on its API library page
facts.text: BLPAPI (core API: C++, Java, C#/.NET), Desktop API (for terminal users), Server API and B-PIPE (server-side data feed), Data License

“100B+ data points published daily”, “100M+ financial instruments”, “47k+ data fields”, “8k+ datasets”: reference, ESG, pricing, risk, regulation, fundamentals, estimates, historical. Delivered by REST API, SFTP, web services or cloud. A self-service portal lets clients browse, test and customise datasets

facts.topic: Data License Plus and Enterprise MCP
facts.text: Adds cloud data sharing, Bloomberg Enterprise MCP and the Qube Datastore with Python access. The MCP covers “more than 100 million securities and over 30,000 fields”, structured by issuer, portfolio and hierarchy. How agents authenticate is not stated on that page
The two pages give different field counts (47k+ for Data License, 30,000+ for the MCP). I did not check why

A managed MCP server announced with Microsoft, to connect Copilot Studio to LSEG APIs; and a first phase in Databricks Marketplace through Agent Bricks and Delta Sharing: LSEG Financial Analytics, Lipper Fund Data and Analytics, Historical Analytics. “AI-ready content will continue to roll out in phases through MCP”

LSEG Data Library (Python, TypeScript, .NET): a desktop session needs the Workspace or Eikon app running locally plus an app key; a platform session needs an app key and user credentials. Datastream Web Service for time-series data. Eikon Data API is described as “very unlikely” to be needed

“M&A, private equity, capital raising, infrastructure, company events”; 4.4 million+ deals, 1.5 million+ M&A transactions, back to 1960. Desktop access through Workspace, SDC and DBI; an SFTP feed per dataset; the LSEG data catalogue

No vendor called “DealInfo”. “Contexa” matched three unrelated things: a WooCommerce search product (contexa.co), a document-extraction API (contexa.works) and an MCP developer platform (contexaai.com). None is a financial-data vendor, so I did not guess

patterns.text: Crunchbase, ZoomInfo, Moody's and S&P/Kensho all have the person sign in with their own vendor account (OAuth or a vendor login)

patterns.pattern: An account or licence comes first
patterns.text: Crunchbase needs an MCP seat, ZoomInfo a licence (a trial is offered), Moody's credentials issued by Moody's, LSEG an LSEG product licence, and Bloomberg Data License Plus is requested through a demo form

patterns.pattern: An API usually exists beside the MCP
patterns.text: Crunchbase, ZoomInfo, Bloomberg and LSEG each also publish REST or library APIs. For Moody's and S&P Kensho the page names APIs but gives no endpoints

patterns.pattern: Not every dataset is reachable by an agent
patterns.text: SharkRepellent, S&P ratings and Fitch have no endpoint on the pages I could read
None of the pages read states a price; every vendor sends you to sales or a demo

nextStep: **Next step for the agent:** the MCP client on pages D2.3.1 and D2.3.2 connects to one MCP server by URL (Streamable HTTP) or by command (stdio). A vendor server that signs the user in with OAuth is the same client with a different URL and a sign-in step; this workbench's client does not do that sign-in yet.

No page states a price, a contract term or a licence tier for any vendor.
“DealInfo” and “Contexa” could not be identified as financial-data vendors.
